name: Sampling distribution of the sample mean
quote: If the population is approximately normal, or if the sample size is large enough (at least 30) for the central limit theorem to apply, we also have that the set of sample means is approximately normally distributed.
plain_en: distribution of sample means over repeated samples

name: Mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean
quote: The mean of the set of sample means equals
plain_en: sample means average to population mean

name: Standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean
quote: The standard deviation of the set of sample means is approximately equal to
plain_en: population SD divided by square root n

name: Normality condition for means
quote: The normality condition: Either the population distribution should be approximately normal or the sample size n should be ≥ 30, or if n < 30, the sample data should be free from strong skewness and outliers.
plain_en: normal population or large sample or symmetric data

name: t-distribution
quote: with a resulting t-distribution that is bell-shaped and symmetric but lower at the mean, higher at the tails, and so more spread out than the normal distribution.
plain_en: bell-shaped distribution with heavier tails

name: Degrees of freedom
quote: In the tables, these distinct t-distributions are associated with the values for degrees of freedom (df). For this discussion, the df value is equal to the sample size minus 1.
plain_en: sample size minus one for one-sample t

name: When to use the t-distribution
quote: Thus, the t-distribution is the proper choice whenever the population standard deviation σ is unknown.
plain_en: use t when population SD is unknown

name: Critical value t*
quote: where the critical value, t*, depends on the chosen confidence level and on the degrees of freedom, df = n – 1.
plain_en: t multiplier for confidence level and df

name: One-sample t-interval for a population mean
quote: Naming the procedure is easiest done by simply stating “one-sample t-interval for a population mean.”
plain_en: confidence interval for one mean

name: One-sample t-interval for a population mean difference
quote: For this matched pairs design, the procedure is called a “one-sample t-interval for a population mean difference.”
plain_en: interval for mean of paired differences

name: One-sample t-test for a population mean
quote: Procedure: A one-sample t-test for a population mean (population SD is unknown)
plain_en: hypothesis test for one mean

name: One-sample t-test for a population mean difference
quote: Procedure: A one-sample t-test for a population mean difference (the mean difference of reaction times, before minus after)
plain_en: hypothesis test for paired differences

name: Mean of the difference in sample means
quote: The mean of the set of differences of sample means equals the difference of population means.
plain_en: difference averages to population difference

name: Standard deviation of the difference in sample means
quote: The standard deviation of the set of differences of sample means is approximately equal to
plain_en: spread of difference between sample means

name: Normality of the difference in sample means
quote: If the populations are normal or if the sample sizes are large enough (at least 30) for the central limit theorem to apply, we also have that the set of all differences of sample means is approximately normally distributed.
plain_en: difference of means is approximately normal

quote: The confidence interval takes the following form:
plain_en: interval estimate for difference of two means

name: Null hypothesis for two means
quote: The null hypothesis is usually that the means of the populations are the same or, equivalently, that their difference is 0:
plain_en: hypothesis that two population means are equal

name: Alternative hypothesis for two means
quote: The alternative hypothesis is then:
plain_en: hypothesis that the two means differ

name: Two-sample t-test for a difference of means
quote: Procedure: A two-sample t-test for the difference of two population means
plain_en: hypothesis test comparing two means

name: No pooling in a two-sample t-test
quote: You should not pool in a two-sample t-test like we did in a two- proportion z- test.
plain_en: do not pool standard deviations for two means

name: Simulation p-value
quote: We can use a simulation to determine what values of a test statistic are likely to occur by random chance alone, assuming the null hypothesis is true. Then looking at where our test statistic falls, we can estimate a p-value.
plain_en: estimate p-value from simulated statistics

name: Power given a specific alternative
quote: Given a specific alternative hypothesis, a Type II error is a mistaken failure to reject the false null hypothesis, while the power is the probability of rejecting that false null hypothesis.
plain_en: probability of rejecting a false null

name: Factors that increase power
quote: A general conclusion is that if the other three values below are unchanged, the power will increase (and the probability of a Type II error will decrease) if any of the following occur:
plain_en: power rises with alpha, n, effect, lower SE

name: Effect size
quote: The difference between p0 and p is sometimes called the effect—thus the greater the effect, the greater is the power.
plain_en: distance between null and true parameter

name: Choosing a confidence interval
quote: An estimate of an unknown population parameter indicates a confidence interval.
plain_en: estimate requested means use interval

name: Choosing a hypothesis test
quote: A claim about a population parameter indicates a hypothesis test.
plain_en: claim requested means use hypothesis test

name: Confidence interval and hypothesis test consistency
quote: If a 95% confidence interval for μ captures μ0, there is not sufficient evidence to reject H0 : μ = μ0 in a two-sided test with α = 0.05.
plain_en: interval containing null value matches non-rejection
